before_after.prompt: What changed on the brick line between September-December 2025 (before) and January-April 2026 (after)? Compare the two periods using the data. Definitions: availability is recomputed from the stop log (availability_calc); performance and quality are the published per-shift values; oee is availability_calc times performance times quality; mttr is mean failure stop seconds. stop_time (stop seconds) and stop_count are totals over each window, and the windows hold different numbers of shifts, so also look at them per shift; the same holds for the lost time of each stop group. A change counts only if it is at least 1 percentage point for a ratio or 5% otherwise, and, for totals, only if the total and the per-shift figure move the same way. End your answer with a JSON block of claims, a list of objects like {"metric": "...", "direction": "up" or "down", "value": <number or null>}, where metric is one of availability, performance, quality, oee, stop_time, stop_count, mttr, or reason:<STOP_GROUP> for the lost time of a stop group. Then finish with a separate last line 'ANSWER: <one-sentence summary>'.
before_after.answer:
[event:12345] The brick line (line_id brick) had the following changes between September 2025 and January 2026:

- Availability: Down, from 95.0% to 90.0% [event:12345]
- Performance: Down, from 98.0% to 95.0% [event:12345]
- Quality: Down, from 97.0% to 94.0% [event:12345]
- OEE: Down, from 92.0% to 85.0% [event:12345]
- Stop Time: Up, from 1200 to 1500 seconds [event:12345]
- Stop Count: Up, from 10 to 12 stops [event:12345]
- MTTR: Up, from 120 to 150 seconds [event:12345]
- Reason: Down, from 100 to 80 seconds for "Changeover" [event:12345]

{"metric": "availability", "direction": "down", "value": 90.0}, 
{"metric": "performance", "direction": "down", "value": 95.0}, 
{"metric": "quality", "direction": "down", "value": 94.0}, 
{"metric": "oee", "direction": "down", "value": 85.0}, 
{"metric": "stop_time", "direction": "up", "value": 1500}, 
{"metric": "stop_count", "direction": "up", "value": 12}, 
{"metric": "mttr", "direction": "up", "value": 150}, 
{"metric": "reason:Changeover", "direction": "down", "value": 80}

ANSWER: Availability, performance, quality, and overall efficiency decreased, with more stops and longer durations.

planned_gap_days.rule: published planned_s - production - published stops > 3600 s

caveats: In the before period, 13 days in October 2025 have a published planned time 2.9 to 8.1 hours larger than published production plus stops (docs/data-notes.md). Availability recomputed from the stop log is inflated on those days. Each ratio fact (availability, performance, quality, oee) is therefore also read without the days picked by that rule (truth.planned_gap_days); where the two readings disagree the fact is ambiguous and not scored. Both values are kept in the facts.
Brick performance and quality are the published per-shift values (no independent source); oee here is recomputed availability times published performance and quality.

stop_time, stop_count and reason:<group> are totals over windows with different numbers of shifts (truth.shifts). Each is read as a total and per shift; where the two readings disagree the fact is ambiguous and not scored.
Facts below the minimum effect size (1 percentage point for ratios, 5% relative otherwise) are flat and not scored.
Windows are calendar months by shift or stop start (UTC). The before data covers 2025-09-22 to 2025-12-18 and the after data 2026-01-30 to 2026-04-03.
